title: Control an unbounded port moment using all-band heat traces and nearby-spring partitions
statement: The isolated spring-confined rotor and, separately, its full live-lead contact have uniform true Gibbs Var(Y) bounds in the fixed-I large-g, k=kappa/B, beta=sB family. The loaded contact approaches the dressed Gaussian state on bounded records; nearby-stiffness partition ratios separately establish its actual Y^2 limit.

requires: Specified positive spring, actual canonical Gibbs state, all rotor/lead modes, finite pinned regulators followed by the stated local lead and gain limits. Fixed-I increasing-g family with b=(1/4+epsilon)log R, or the separately checked stronger family.
provides: The isolated spring-confined rotor and, separately, its full live-lead contact have uniform true Gibbs Var(Y) bounds in the fixed-I large-g, k=kappa/B, beta=sB family. The loaded contact approaches the dressed Gaussian state on bounded records; nearby-stiffness partition ratios separately establish its actual Y^2 limit.
assumptions: Isolated packet, isolated Gibbs and loaded Gibbs are distinct ensembles. No finite preparation time or dynamics follows from free-energy closeness. The large-I/fixed-g route has a different metric scaling and is not covered by this limit.
costs: Ground energy E_R b, lock resources, state preparation and finite material/control interfaces remain paid. Finite equilibrium excess or bounded port variance does not establish a finite equilibration clock.
contract.units: beta is inverse energy, k is spring stiffness, Var(Y) is length squared; the source-defined s,kappa retain dimensions in beta=sB,k=kappa/B.
contract.obstruction: Replace the invalid small-leakage/trace-distance-to-second-moment transfer with an actual partition/moment argument.

body: For the isolated ensemble shift the exact E_R b ground reference, retain all q and rotor bands in the diamagnetic normal heat trace, and use the full noncommuting Golden-Thompson form sum plus convex log partition. For live leads, Fourier transformation gives an actual magnetic connection; full heat-kernel diamagnetism and the phase-corrected isometry bound the partition and relative entropy. Compare at k and (1-r)k to bound Y^2, then use bounded truncation/Fatou for the matching limit. A small trace distance alone is never used to control an unbounded moment.
